7.1.2.2 Frame reception in slave nodes This section is only applicable to LIN slave nodes. The LIN slave has no knowledge about the scheduling of the LIN master, it solely reacts to received LIN headers reported by the LIN Driver with the header indication callback function LinIf_HeaderIndication. The requirements in this section are applicable to all frame types that are received by the slave. An exception is the MRF for which only the header handling in Chapter 7.1.2.2.1 applies, but the response handling is described in Chapter 7.6.2 and Chapter 7.6.3.

new.text: 9.1.2 Frame transmission in slave nodes This section is only applicable to LIN slave nodes. The following use case (Figure 9.3) shows the transmission of a LIN frame. After a received LIN header is indicated by the LIN driver, the PID is evaluated (shown by function EvaluatePID). If it’s determined to belong to a transmission frame, the trans- mission response data is requested from upper layer. The buffer to which SduPtr member in PduPtr parameter points to can be directly passed to let the upper layer copy the transmission data to the provided buffer. The LIN interface informs the driver about the response type by setting the appropriate members of PduPtr (shown by function SetPduPtrValues). The CopyBuffer call is to show that the copying of the SDU is made in the LIN Driver and not in the LIN Interface. «module» LSduR «module» Lin «module» LinIf «Peripheral» LinController/UART LSduR_LinIfTxConfirmation() LinIf_TxConfirmation() Interrupt() SetPduPtrValues() LinIf_HeaderIndication() LSduR_LinIfTriggerTransmit() Interrupt() CopyBuffer() EvaluatePID() SetupBuffer() Figure 9.3: Frame transmission (slave node)

9.3.2 Irrelevant communication in slave nodes This section is only applicable to LIN slave nodes. The third direction for a LIN frame is that the frame is not relevant for the slave node and is ignored. After a received LIN header is indicated by the LIN driver, the PID is evaluated (shown by function EvaluatePID). If it’s determined to belong to an Irrelevant frame, the LIN interface informs the driver about the response type by setting the appropriate members of PduPtr (shown by function SetPduPtrValues).
